Woman
WOOM-'n
n. (rendering Hebrew 'ishshâh, Greek gunē)
From Old English wīfman, a compound of wīf (woman, wife) and man (human being) — so that the English word preserves, by accident, the very structure of Gen 2:23. The Hebrew does it deliberately and audibly: the man is 'īsh and the woman is 'ishshâh, and Adam's naming is a pun no translation can carry — she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man. The name is itself a doctrine of origin, distinction, and correspondence.

Biblical Definition

Woman is a creational category, given by God, embodied, and not self-assigned. She is made last and made deliberately, not from the ground as the man was but from the man himself, so that her origin declares both her equality of nature and her distinctness of person: “And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man” (Gen 2:22). She bears the image of God fully and equally — male and female created he them — and she is given an order within that equality, for the man was not created for the woman, but the woman for the man. The fall came through her deception, which Scripture records without excusing the man, who was not deceived and yet ate: “And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression” (1Ti 2:14). Yet the first promise of the gospel is spoken to her adversary about her offspring: “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel” (Gen 3:15). The whole redemptive line runs through the seed of the woman, and it terminates in an event described in exactly those terms: “God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law” (Gal 4:4). The dignity Scripture assigns to woman is therefore not honorary. It is a share in the image, a distinct calling, and the instrument through which the Redeemer entered the world. And her praise is located where the world never looks for it: “Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised” (Pro 31:30).

Webster 1828 Definition

The female of the human race, made by God from the man and for the man, equally an image-bearer with him; and in Scripture the one through whose seed the Redeemer was promised and of whom the Son of God was made.

WOMAN, n. 1. The female of the human race, grown to adult years.

2. A female attendant or servant; also, the sex taken collectively; as, woman is the glory of the man. 1 Cor. 11.

3. In the Hebrew, ishshah, so called from ish, man, because she was taken out of man. Gen. 2.

4. A wife; as, the woman of a household. Every man shall have his own wife. 1 Cor. 7.

5. In Scripture, the seed of the woman shall bruise the serpent's head. Gen. 3. Made of a woman, made under the law. Gal. 4.

Key Scripture

Genesis 2:22 — "And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man."

Genesis 3:15 — "And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel."

Proverbs 31:30 — "Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised."

Galatians 4:4 — "But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law,"

Modern Corruption

Womanhood is severed from the body and redefined as an inward identity anyone may claim, so that the creational category of Genesis 1:27 is emptied; and in the opposite direction, the woman's equal bearing of the divine image is denied in practice by contempt or domination.

expand to see more

The governing modern corruption is the claim that woman names an inward sense of identity rather than an embodied creational reality — that the category is assigned rather than given, and can therefore be adopted, exited, or held by anyone who declares it. Scripture's account is unambiguous and it is an account of bodies: God made them male and female, made the woman from the man's side, and the Lord Jesus grounds His teaching on marriage in the fact that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female. This is not a cultural convention that Genesis happens to report; it is presented as the act of the Creator, and it is the premise of the marriage covenant, of the promise of the woman's seed, and of the incarnation itself, in which the Son was made of a woman. A category which can be claimed at will cannot bear any of that weight. The dictionary affirms the image of God in every person who suffers under this confusion, and refuses the framework precisely because the framework cannot give them what they were made for.

The opposite corruption is older and has done its own great damage: the denial in practice of the woman's equal standing before God. Where Scripture says male and female created he them, in the image of God, some have inferred from the order of creation a difference of worth, and treated headship as licence for contempt, domination, or neglect. The apostles forbid the inference explicitly. Husbands are commanded to love their wives as Christ loved the church and gave himself for it, to dwell with them according to knowledge, and to honour them as heirs together of the grace of life — with the striking sanction that failure here obstructs a man's prayers. The principle to recover holds both truths at once: equal in nature, dignity, and inheritance; distinct in creation, calling, and order. Scripture never trades one for the other, and every corruption of this doctrine is an attempt to be rid of one half.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew 'ishshâh is woman or wife, formed from 'īsh, man, and preserving the pun of Gen 2:23. Greek gunē means woman or wife according to context, and thēlus is the female as a creational category in Gen 1:27 and Mat 19:4.

expand to see more

Hebrew 'ishshâh (H802) — woman, wife, female; named from 'īsh, man, because she was taken out of man (Gen 2:23).

Hebrew n'qēbâh (H5347) — female, the creational counterpart to zākār, male; male and female created he them (Gen 1:27).

Hebrew 'ēzer k'negdō — a help meet for him, literally a helper corresponding to him; 'ēzer is elsewhere used of God Himself as Israel's help.

Greek gunē (G1135) — woman or wife; made of a woman, made under the law (Gal 4:4).

Greek thēlus (G2338) — female; used by Christ in Mat 19:4 quoting Genesis, and by Paul in Gal 3:28 of standing in Christ.

Usage

"Of her creation and correspondence: the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman (Gen 2:22)."

"Of the promise through her seed: I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed (Gen 3:15)."

"Of the praise Scripture assigns her: a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised (Pro 31:30)."
